s1.syndrome_frame: Acute limb ischemia with aneurysm and hematoma
salient_findings: Swollen right knee and thigh with extensive bruising
Pulsatile mass extending into the mid-thigh
key_facts: 96-year-old man with benign prostatic disease and dementia
Presented after a collapse at home
Normocytic anemia (hemoglobin 119 g/L) on admission
D-dimer of 1095 ng/mL on admission
Neutrophilia (10.44 × 10^9/L) on admission
Initial diagnosis of venous thromboembolism was excluded
Discharged with antibiotics for a presumed urinary tract infection
Returned with a swollen right knee and thigh and extensive bruising
Lower limb ultrasound showed a patent venous system
45 mm popliteal artery aneurysm with an 11.4 × 5.2 cm medial leg hematoma
Worsening right-leg pain and difficulty walking on subsequent admission
Extensive bruising behind the right knee and posterior-medial thigh
Pulseless right foot without signs of acute ischemia
Repeat hemoglobin was 77 g/L
Computed tomography angiography demonstrated a 4 × 5 cm saccular popliteal artery aneurysm

shortlist.label: Popliteal artery aneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a confirmed 4 × 5 cm saccular popliteal artery aneurysm with a large posterior thigh collection

shortlist.label: Peripheral artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has severely diseased but patent runoff vessels, indicating possible peripheral artery disease

shortlist.label: Thromboangiitis obliterans
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age and presentation with limb ischemia and aneurysm could be consistent with thromboangiitis obliterans

shortlist.label: Fibromuscular dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's aneurysm and vascular disease could be related to fibromuscular dysplasia, a rare but possible cause

shortlist.label: Buerger's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation with limb ischemia, aneurysm, and hematoma could be consistent with Buerger's disease, a rare but clinically plausible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a swollen right knee and thigh, extensive bruising, and a pulseless right foot, combined with imaging findings of a 4 × 5 cm saccular popliteal artery aneurysm, strongly supports this diagnosis

rejected.label: Peripheral artery disease
rejected.why: While the patient has severely diseased runoff vessels, the primary issue is the aneurysm, not the disease of the peripheral arteries

rejected.label: Thromboangiitis obliterans
rejected.why: This condition typically affects younger patients and is associated with tobacco use, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Fibromuscular dysplasia
rejected.why: This condition is more common in younger women and typically affects the renal and internal carotid arteries, not the popliteal artery

rejected.label: Buerger's disease
rejected.why: This condition is also associated with tobacco use and typically affects the distal arteries of the limbs, but the patient's presentation and imaging findings are more consistent with a popliteal artery aneurysm
